newsitem.title: UK: Moody's cuts National Power snr debt to A2.
newsitem.headline: Moody's cuts National Power snr debt to A2.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service said on Monday it had downgraded the senior debt ratings of National Power Plc to A2 from Aa3.

"These downgrades are based on Moody's expectation that business risk will increase and cash flow quality deteriorate as the company undertakes a substantial overseas investment programme financed mainly by debt to provide the potential for long term profits growth," Moody's said in statement.
It said the rating action concluded a review initiated in August 1996 and added that National Power's Prime 1 short-term rating for commercial paper was not on review and was confirmed.

"National Power has set out to build a significant overseas generation investment portfolio in a comparatively short time in order to provide longer term profits growth when its domestic business faces revenue pressures on full de-regulation of UK energy supply slated for 1998," Moody's said.

"The company's track record in the relatively immature overseas power project market is comparatively short and its most significant investment to date, its shareholding in Hazelwood Power, made as recently as August of last year."

The agency said it considered National Power's management would structure transactions relatively prudently to protect the company against non-operating risks but fierce competition for attractive energy projects would increase financial risk.

"In addition to a large increase in debt as National Power undertakes its substantial investment programme, Moody's expects the company's investments to be highly leveraged with, in the main, non recourse debt," it said.

"In view of the importance to the company of cash flows from its portfolio of overseas investments, Moody's regards the non-recourse debt as a moderate use of debt capacity and has factored this appropriately into its assessment of National Power's credit profile," it added.

Moody's said it would monitor the firm's developing international project business and said the ratings anticipated that the company would achieve planned returns from a balanced portfolio of power projects in emerging and developed economies.
"Failure to do so could have further negative rating implications," it said.
